title: CmdPal: Add a Charts and visuals sample page and author docs

proposed_comments.title: Distinguish the Charts sample in command telemetry
proposed_comments.body:
### Distinguish the Charts sample in command telemetry

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/SamplePagesExtension/Pages/SampleChartsPage.cs:20`.

**Problem:** This page and the existing `OnLoadPage` both use the command name `Open` and an empty command ID within the Samples extension. The telemetry path records the extension ID, command ID, and command name—not the separate page title—so these invocations are indistinguishable.

**Why it matters:** Usage telemetry cannot tell whether users opened the Charts and visuals page or the existing OnLoadPage sample.

**Suggested change:**
```suggestion
        Name = "Charts and visuals";
```

**Verification:** Confirm the Charts and visuals invocation has a distinct command name from OnLoadPage.

confidence.rationale: The same registered extension emits identical Id and Name fields for these two commands; the telemetry payload is directly visible at the pinned caller.

proposed_comments.title: Make the author-guide reference clickable
proposed_comments.body:
### Make the author-guide reference clickable

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.AdaptiveCards.Polyfills/README.md:20`.

**Problem:** The new guide is written as a Windows-style path in code formatting, so readers cannot open it from the README.

**Why it matters:** Extension authors must locate the new authoring guidance manually instead of following the README reference.

**Suggested change:**
```suggestion
Extension authors: see [charts-and-visuals.md](../ExtensionTemplate/TemplateCmdPalExtension/.github/skills/add-adaptive-card-form/references/charts-and-visuals.md), and the Samples extension's "Charts and visuals" page.
```

**Verification:** Confirm the relative Markdown link resolves to the added guide.

confidence.rationale: The exact README source line and the target guide both exist at the pinned head; the relative link resolves to that target.
